newsitem.title: ITALY: BCI has cash to spend, wary on 97 profit.
newsitem.headline: BCI has cash to spend, wary on 97 profit.

text.p: Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) has over three trillion lire to invest in shareholdings and is closely watching out for market opportunities, managing director Luigi Fausti said.
"We have an available margin of 3.368 trillion lire, of which we can spend over three trillion on shareholdings," Fausti told the bank's annual shareholders' meeting.
"BCI feels it has a duty to watch the market in order to pick out opportunities," he added.
He said 1997 had started out well as far as deposits and loans were concerned but he was cautious about forecasting profits for this year.

As of March 10, BCI's direct customer deposits were up 8.7 percent, customer loans up 7.3 percent and administered customer assets up 16.6 percent to around 200 trillion lire, he said without elaborating.
"The 1997 budget is above that for 1996 but three percent lower than the actual budget implemented last year. However, we do not exclude that the bottom line may be above that of 1996," he said.
"But I feel I have to be cautious. I cannot confirm that the second half of this year will show any great economic development," he added.
BCI posted 1996 consolidated net profit of 378 billion lire compared to 365 billion lire in 1995 while parent company net profit was 341 billion lire against 342.3 billion.
